data.hypothesis: The selected SSE2 parent was correct at 5.631 ms versus the 7.529 ms baseline, but it retains per-lane logf and expf calls. This experiment replaces those calls in the guarded four-option SSE2 path with range-reduced vector approximations, retaining the supplied Black-Scholes computation and CND coefficients and falling back to the scalar loop for unsafe blocks and tails. It tests whether removing scalar transcendental calls improves throughput; correctness and speed remain for the controller to measure.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this SSE2 path, scalar transcendental calls remain a plausible cost to test; unsafe input ranges should stay on the scalar path.
memory_lessons.claim: The selected explicit SSE2 program was measured correct at 5.631 ms, compared with the 7.529 ms baseline. This is a measured result, not proof that scalar math calls caused the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a guarded explicit kernel that vectorizes log and exp while retaining scalar fallbacks.

memory_lessons.applicability: This supports testing vectorized transcendental math, but does not establish that this implementation or its approximations will be faster or accurate enough.
memory_lessons.claim: A separate full-SSE2 candidate was measured correct at 2.662 ms; it is the best recorded T2 result in the supplied catalog.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this candidate's correctness and repeated timings against the selected parent and ordinary baseline.

data.notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is proposed for change. The source retains a scalar fallback for unsupported builds, unsafe vector blocks, and tails; no runtime ISA probing or compiler-flag change is proposed. No new performance or correctness result is claimed.
transformations: Added SSE2 vector log via exponent/mantissa decomposition and an atanh-series polynomial; guarded its input to positive finite normal ratios.
Added SSE2 vector exp via range reduction and a degree-eight polynomial; unsafe argument ranges fall back to the ordinary scalar implementation.
Applied the vector math to the explicit four-option Black-Scholes kernel while preserving the supplied CND coefficients and computation order.
Retained the scalar loop for unsupported builds, unsafe four-option blocks, and vector tails; left threading, the run contract, and build flags unchanged.
